name: Great Himalayan National Park
opening_hours: Sunrise to Sunset · Trekking requires forest department permit
best_time: April to June and September to November
rules: Forest department entry permit mandatory at Sai Ropa or Sainj office
Strict no-plastic and no-fire zone in core wilderness area
visual_features: virgin alpine river valley flanked by rugged crags, wildflower meadows, and pristine glacier-fed streams
description: The Great Himalayan National Park (GHNP) is a national park in India, located in Banjar sub-division of Kullu in the state of Himachal Pradesh. The park was established in 1984 and is spread over an area of 1171 km2; elevations within the park range between 1500 and 6000 m. The Great Himalayan National Park is a habitat to numerous flora and more than 375 fauna species, including approximately 31 mammals, 181 birds, 3 reptiles, 9 amphibians, 11 annelids, 17 mollusks and 127 insects. They are protected under the strict guidelines of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972; hence any sort of hunting is not permitted.
